idScheme.allocation: RVL-GAP- followed by a zero-padded slot number. The slot is allocated in this file and names a capability Ravel would provide, never an entry that would use it.
idScheme.native: The id, like every other string a proposal record carries, is Ravel's own. No proposal names an acquired file, a project id, a file id, or any word an upstream project chose.

minimumMotivatingEntries.rule: A capability proposal is admissible only where the entries whose counted surfaces motivate it number at least this many.
minimumMotivatingEntries.judgement: the edge. Twenty is under a tenth of the acquired set and well above the largest single dependency cluster, so a pattern that clears it is carried by entries that share nothing but the surface they declare. Below it, what looks like a platform gap is more cheaply read as a habit of a few entries, and the right answer is one counterpart rather than a capability every mod pays for.

motivationRules.any: An entry motivates the proposal when at least one cited surface family is nonzero for it.
motivationRules.all: An entry motivates the proposal when every cited surface family is nonzero for it.

dispositions.proposed: At least one proposal in this file cites the family as motivation.
dispositions.shipped: The public SDK already exposes a module that answers the family, so the family is not a gap. The named module has to exist in the public checkout for the claim to stand.
dispositions.not-a-capability: The family is a size proxy rather than a thing a mod declares, so no capability answers it and none is proposed. The rubric already treats it as a band rather than as a measurement.

estimateDisclosure: Two families are estimates rather than findings: they count classes on a path whose name suggests a purpose, because what registers a packet or a saved-data table is code this workspace does not read. Both are dispositioned shipped rather than proposed, so no proposal in this file rests on an estimate. A record that cited one would carry restsOnEstimate true, and the consumer recomputes that flag rather than believing it.

testCaseKinds.declaration-accepted: A well-formed declaration is taken, and what it produces is what the capability promises.
testCaseKinds.conflict-refused: A second claim on one owned thing is refused, and the refusal names both claimants.
testCaseKinds.generation-determinism: The same declaration produces the same bytes twice.
testCaseKinds.ordering: Two declarations that depend on each other are entered in the order the dependency implies, and a cycle is refused.
testCaseKinds.side-refusal: A declaration only one side may make is refused on the other side rather than quietly skipped.
testCaseKinds.absent-dependency-refused: A declaration naming something no installed mod provides is refused at the barrier rather than at first use.
testCaseKinds.round-trip: A value written by the capability is read back equal, and a value the capability did not write is refused.

testCaseOrigin.rule: Every test case is written against the proposed Ravel capability. None is transcribed or adapted from any other project's tests.
testCaseOrigin.mechanism: The bound is the same structural one the reference records rest on rather than a promise. No producer in this workspace has ever opened a test belonging to an acquired entry, so there is nothing here to transcribe from. What holds it is the closed lexicon: every word in every proposal file, test cases included, has to appear in checks/proposals-lexicon.txt, and that lexicon is required to share nothing with the identifiers the inventory knows. A transcribed test would arrive carrying words nobody added to the lexicon, and a lexicon edited to admit them would fail against the same identifier set.

server-data-declaration.capability: A mod declares the server-resolved data entries it owns in the one declaration that already holds its registry keys, tag memberships and translations, so that one barrier answers whether a path is already claimed and one generation step writes the same bytes every run.
server-data-declaration.whyGeneral: Entries of this shape are carried across every lane the inventory assigns, and by a majority of the acquired set rather than by one kind of entry. The public SDK declares registry keys, tag memberships, translations and bytes a mod supplies itself; a server-resolved entry is none of those, so today it can only be shipped as supplied bytes, which is the escape hatch the declaration itself treats as a last resort.
server-data-declaration.boundary: The proposal is the declaration and the refusal. It specifies no entry's tables and reproduces nothing any entry ships.

world-shaping-declaration.capability: A mod declares how it shapes a world, and Ravel binds that declaration to the world once, at creation, so a world records which shaping mods were in force when it was made and refuses a later launch that no longer supplies one.
world-shaping-declaration.whyGeneral: The family is declared by enough of the acquired set to clear the threshold, and it is the one content family whose effect is written into a world rather than resolved per launch. The SDK versions the data a mod owns and migrates it, but nothing binds a world to the set of mods that shaped it, so removing one is silent where removing owned data is not.
world-shaping-declaration.boundary: The proposal is the binding and the refusal, not any generator, biome, or placement an entry defines.

audio-declaration.capability: A mod declares the audio entries it owns and the events that play them, as a declaration whose client half is refused on a server rather than skipped there.
audio-declaration.whyGeneral: The family clears the threshold across entries whose lanes and rights differ, so it is not one lane's need. The SDK can carry the bytes as a supplied resource, but it has no entry kind for an audio event, so nothing relates the bytes to what plays them and nothing refuses a play call made on the wrong side.
audio-declaration.boundary: No audio is reproduced, described, or carried. The proposal is the entry kind and the side rule.

render-stage-declaration.capability: A mod declares the named drawing stages it contributes to and the order it wants among other mods at each one, and Ravel refuses a cycle and a stage no mod declares rather than resolving either quietly.
render-stage-declaration.whyGeneral: The family clears the threshold, and every entry carrying it is doing the same thing structurally: adding work to a stage some other party also draws in. Ordering between mods is what the SDK already solved for named calls between mods, and drawing has none of it.
render-stage-declaration.boundary: No drawing program is written, ported, or described. The proposal is the stage name, the ordering, and the two refusals.

behaviour-interception.capability: A mod declares that it wants to answer at a named point in the game rather than only to be told what happened there, and Ravel publishes those points, orders the mods at each one, and lets a mod refuse or replace the outcome under a declared contract.
behaviour-interception.whyGeneral: This is the largest pattern in the inventory by entry count and it spans every lane. The SDK tells a mod what the game did; it has no way for a mod to change what the game is about to do. Nothing about the pattern is one entry's: what differs between entries is which point they want, and a point is exactly what a platform can publish once.
behaviour-interception.boundary: The proposal is a published set of points with an ordering and a refusal contract. It is not a way to rewrite the game's code, it names no point any entry chose, and it reproduces no entry's behaviour.
behaviour-interception.restraint: Ravel forbids unsafe code in every maintained crate and this proposal does not ask for an exception. A point is a place the host already calls out from, so an interception is a call the host makes, not a patch a mod applies.

library-provision.capability: A mod declares that it provides a shared library other mods may build on, at a version, and Ravel resolves one provider per library for a launch and refuses a set where two providers disagree or where a required library has none.
library-provision.whyGeneral: Entries carrying this family are each shipping a copy of something meant to be shared, and the count clears the threshold across lanes. The SDK orders named calls between mods that are both installed, which is a different question from which mod supplies a shared thing and at what version. Nothing today answers the second.
library-provision.boundary: No library is ported, bundled, or named. The proposal is the provider declaration, the resolution, and the two refusals.
